sheets.title: Delhi Sultanate (1206 – 1526)
sheets.intro: Ghori to Ibrahim Lodi: Sultans, reforms, government, buildings, books.

rows.v: 712 CE
Muhammad bin Qasim (nephew, son-in-law of Hajjaj, Iraq) beat Dahir; took Debal
Chachnama (Persian, Ali Kufi)
Pratihara Nagabhata I, Bappa Rawal (Mewar), Chalukyas
977 – 997; founder; beat Hindushahi Jayapala
998 – 1030; 17 raids 1000 – 1027 – Waihind (Anandapala 1008 – 09), Kannauj 1018, Somnath 1025
Alberuni – Kitab-ul-Hind; Firdausi – Shahnama; Utbi – Tarikh-i-Yamini
Took Ghazni 1173; Gomal pass; Multan, Uch 1175; Lahore 1186 (last Ghaznavid Khusrau Malik)
Kayadara 1178 (Solankis); Tarain I 1191 (Prithviraj) over Bhatinda
Tarain II 1192 (mounted archers, Rajput disunity); Chandawar 1194 (Jaichandra)
Bihar, Bengal; sacked Nalanda, Vikramashila, Odantapuri; surprised Lakshmana Sena at Nadia (c. 1204); base Lakhnauti
Lost to the Khwarizm Shah
1206, Damyak (Jhelum), by Khokhars
Aibak (Delhi, Lahore), Yalduz (Ghazni), Qubacha (Multan, Sindh)
1206 – 1210; first Sultan; Slave (Mamluk) dynasty; court at Lahore
Lakh Baksh (giver of lakhs)
Quwwat-ul-Islam (first Delhi mosque; 27 temples' remains); Adhai Din ka Jhonpra (Ajmer); began Qutb Minar (for Sufi Bakhtiyar Kaki)
Hasan Nizami – Taj-ul-Maasir
Polo (chaugan) fall, Lahore
Aram Shah (1210 – 11)

keys.name: Iltutmish

rows.v: 1211 – 1236; Ilbari Turk; Aibak's slave and son-in-law; real consolidator
Beat Aram Shah at Jud; Yalduz at Tarain (1216); Qubacha drowned (1228)
Refused shelter to Mangbarni (1221) – Chengiz Khan turned back
Recognised by Abbasid al-Mustansir, 1229
Lahore → Delhi
Silver tanka (175 grains), copper jital (48 to a tanka)
Iqta; Turkan-i-Chihalgani (Forty)
Finished Qutb Minar; Sultan Ghari (1231) – first Islamic tomb in India; Hauz-i-Shamsi
Named daughter Razia

traps: Sultan Ghari = first tomb; Quwwat-ul-Islam = first mosque

rows.v: 1236 – 1240; only woman on the Delhi throne
Male dress (qaba, kulah); held open court
Nobles disliked her raising Abyssinian Jamaluddin Yaqut (master of stables)
Married Malik Altunia (Bhatinda); killed near Kaithal 1240
Bahram Shah – nobles made the Naib-i-Mamlakat post

keys.name: Nasiruddin Mahmud

rows.v: Simple; copied the Quran for a living
Balban (Ulugh Khan) ran the state
Minhaj-us-Siraj – Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (named after him)

traps: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is named for Nasiruddin Mahmud

keys.name: Ghiyasuddin Balban

rows.v: "Blood and iron"; Zill-i-Ilahi (shadow of God); Niyabat-i-Khudai; sijda and paibos; Persian festival Nauroz
Broke the Forty (Chihalgani)
Diwan-i-Arz (military department)
Crushed Tughril Beg (Bengal)
Prince Muhammad (Multan; patron of Amir Khusrau) killed by Mongols 1285
Mehrauli – first true arch
Kaiqubad (Kilokhri), Kayumars – end 1290

traps: Diwan-i-Arz = Balban; Diwan-i-Riyasat = Alauddin; Diwan-i-Kohi = MBT

rows.v: 1290 – 1296; "Khalji revolution" – power beyond the old Turkish nobles
Kilokhri
Mild; Mongol converts settled near Delhi ("New Muslims", Mughalpura)
Killed by nephew Alauddin after the Devagiri raid (1296)
Amir Khusrau – Miftah-ul-Futuh

keys.name: Alauddin Khalji

rows.v: 1296 – 1316; title Sikandar-i-Sani; dreamt of a new religion

Gujarat 1299 (Ulugh Khan, Nusrat Khan beat Karna Vaghela; Malik Kafur captured at Cambay); Ranthambore 1301 (Hammir Deva); Chittor 1303 (Ratan Singh; renamed Khizrabad); Malwa 1305; Siwana 1308; Jalore 1311
Beat many raids; Siri fort built during Targhi's siege (1303)
Devagiri 1307 – 08; Warangal 1309 – 10; Dwarasamudra 1311; Madurai 1311 – tribute, not annexation
Alai Darwaza 1311 (first true dome); Hauz-i-Alai (Hauz Khas); unfinished Alai Minar
Amir Khusrau – Khazain-ul-Futuh

traps: Padmini story is from Jayasi’s Padmavat (1540), much later

rows.v: Fixed prices; Mandi (grain), Sarai Adl (cloth); Shahna-i-Mandi; Diwan-i-Riyasat; spies
Standing army paid in cash; Dagh (branding horses), Chehra (soldier's roll)
Half the crop by measurement (masahat, biswa unit); Diwan-i-Mustakhraj (arrears)
Ghari (house), Charai (grazing)
Khuts, muqaddams, chaudharis lost privileges
Banned feasts, marriages without leave; liquor ban
1316 – 1320; only Sultan to call himself Khalifa; softened rules
1320; Baradu convert; "Nasiruddin"; killed by Ghazi Malik
Nuh Sipihr (Mubarak's reign); Ashiqa (Khizr Khan and Deval Rani)
Tuti-i-Hind (parrot of India)
Nizamuddin Auliya (Chishti); buried near him
Five Sultans; Persian and Hindavi
Qiran-us-Sadain (Kaiqubad – Bughra Khan); Miftah-ul-Futuh (Jalaluddin); Khazain-ul-Futuh (Alauddin); Ashiqa; Nuh Sipihr (Mubarak); Tughlaq Nama (Ghiyasuddin)
Qawwali; sitar, tabla linked by tradition only
1320 – 1325; was Ghazi Malik, governor of Dipalpur
Moderation (rasm-i-miyana); first Sultan to dig canals (Barani); roads, post
Tughlaqabad (third city); his tomb – sloping walls
Took it 1323 (Ulugh Khan)
Nizamuddin – "Hunuz Dilli dur ast" (Delhi is still far)
Pavilion fell at Afghanpur, 1325
Capital moved from Delhi to Devagiri 1327; reversed
Bronze / copper at silver value 1329 – 30; forged; withdrawn
Tax raised in famine; peasants fled
Diwan-i-Kohi; taccavi (sondhar) loans
Khurasan (3,70,000 men paid, disbanded); Qarachil (Kumaon) army lost
Jahanpanah (fourth city); Bijai Mandal
Moroccan; qazi of Delhi 8 years (1333 – 42); envoy to China; Rihla
Madurai (1335), Vijayanagara (1336), Bengal (1338), Bahmani (1347)
Thatta 1351 chasing Taghi; Badauni – "freed of his people and they of him"

keys.name: Firoz Shah Tughlaq

rows.v: Only 4 Sharia taxes – Kharaj, Khams (1/5 booty), Jizya (first on Brahmins), Zakat; haq-i-sharb (1/10 irrigation tax)
Yamuna to Hissar; Sutlej to Ghaggar
Firozabad (fifth city, Kotla), Hissar, Jaunpur, Fatehabad
Dar-ul-Shafa (hospital); Diwan-i-Khairat (marriage aid); Diwan-i-Istihqaq (pensions); employment bureau; wrote off taccavi
Diwan-i-Bandagan (about 1,80,000)
Ashokan pillars – Topra to Kotla, Meerut to the Ridge
Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi (own); Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi (Sanskrit texts from Jwalamukhi); Barani and Afif – each a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
Jajnagar (Puri temple desecrated); two failed Bengal campaigns
Hereditary iqtas; Qutb Minar top rebuilt (1368)

traps: Two Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi: Barani and Afif

keys.name: Timur and the end of the Tughlaqs

rows.v: 1398 – Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq's reign
Samarqand ruler; Malfuzat-i-Timuri; sacked Delhi
Khizr Khan governor of Multan
Jaunpur, from 1394 (Malik Sarwar, Malik-us-Sharq)
Timur's governor; title Rayat-i-Ala; ruled in Timur's name
1421 – 34; dropped Timur; first Hindu nobles; Sirhindi – Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi
Octagonal tomb, Lodi Gardens
Retired to Badaun 1451
Descent from the Prophet
1451 – 1526; first Afghan (Pashtun) dynasty
1451 – 89; sat with nobles as equals; copper Bahloli coin; took Jaunpur (c. 1484)
1489 – 1517; pen-name Gulrukhi; founded Agra 1504; Gaz-i-Sikandari (39-digit yard); ended grain duties; tomb – first garden tomb, double dome
1517 – 26; lost to Rana Sanga at Khatoli; harsh to nobles
Daulat Khan Lodi and Alam Khan called Babur
21 April 1526 – only Sultan killed in battle
Octagonal tombs; Bara Gumbad, Moth ki Masjid
Finance – Wazir; Mustaufi (auditor), Mushrif (accountant)
Army – Ariz-i-Mamalik
Letters – Dabir
Religion, grants – Sadr-us-Sudur
Justice – Qazi-ul-Quzat
Intelligence, news
Revenue grant for service (muqti); Iltutmish; forerunner of jagir
Crown land
Iqta → Shiq (shiqdar) → Pargana (amil) → village (muqaddam, chaudhari, patwari)
Kharaj (land), Jizya, Zakat (2.5% on Muslims), Khams (1/5; Alauddin and MBT took 4/5)
About 72.5 m, five storeys; Aibak base, Iltutmish three, Firoz top; UNESCO 1993
Quwwat-ul-Islam
Sultan Ghari (1231)
Balban's tomb
Alai Darwaza (1311)
Sloping walls, grey stone
Octagonal tombs, double domes
Qila Rai Pithora, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Firozabad, Dinpanah (Purana Qila), Shahjahanabad
Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Taj-ul-Maasir (Aibak)
Khazain-ul-Futuh (Alauddin)
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi (Balban to Firoz); Fatawa-i-Jahandari
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi (Firoz's reign)
Futuh-us-Salatin (verse; Bahmani court)
Rihla
Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi
